semantic_correction.stem: A client with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) asks which lifestyle changes are most useful. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Use an individualized plan for healthy weight management, a Mediterranean-style nutrient-dense eating pattern, and regular aerobic or resistance activity while addressing metabolic risk factors.
options.B: Avoid most dietary fat and emphasize carbohydrate intake, because total fat restriction is the main lifestyle treatment for reducing liver fat in MASLD.
options.C: Delay structured diet and activity changes until advanced fibrosis develops, because lifestyle intervention has little effect earlier in the MASLD disease course.
options.D: Focus on weight change alone and leave exercise and cardiometabolic risk factors unchanged, because those measures add little once MASLD has been diagnosed.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current AASLD guidance identifies lifestyle modification as a core part of MASLD management. AASLD describes weight management when appropriate, a hypocaloric dietary pattern with Mediterranean-style features, and regular aerobic or resistance activity as useful approaches, and emphasizes management of cardiometabolic risk factors. B is incorrect because AASLD does not recommend blanket elimination of dietary fat; dietary quality and overall energy balance are more relevant. C is incorrect because lifestyle intervention is used across the MASLD spectrum and is not reserved for advanced fibrosis. D is incorrect because exercise and cardiometabolic risk-factor management remain important components of MASLD care rather than being replaced by weight change alone.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach clients with MASLD that individualized weight management, a healthful dietary pattern, regular physical activity, and management of metabolic risk factors are foundational components of care across the disease spectrum.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests foundational MASLD lifestyle care with one clearly best answer and no answer-length or conspicuous absolute-word cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. Every component is supported by current AASLD MASLD guidance: individualized weight management, healthful dietary change, physical activity, and metabolic risk-factor management.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. AASLD supports dietary-quality and energy-balance changes, not blanket fat elimination or a carbohydrate-focused substitute.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Lifestyle intervention is foundational before advanced fibrosis and is not deferred until late-stage disease.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Exercise and cardiometabolic risk-factor management remain important independent components of MASLD care.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines the major current lifestyle-management domains; B misstates dietary guidance, C improperly delays intervention, and D omits exercise and metabolic-risk management.
cueing_check: All four choices are parallel lifestyle-management plans of comparable length and specificity; no conspicuous absolute word or uniquely long correct answer identifies A.
